rows.grounds: vocative compound addressing the lord of knowledge
compound: devoid of the affliction of discourse about agency etc.
vocative compound addressing the lord of action
compound: abiding as the distinctive state of non-action

items.question: How can the lord of knowledge and action remain free from agency-talk while abiding in non-action?
premises: The lord governs knowledge.
The lord governs action.
Discourse about agency causes distress.
True abiding is excellence of non-action.
items.inference: The supreme lord transcends agency-discourse by resting in the excellence of non-action while still being lord of knowledge and action.
uncertainties: Whether naiṣkarmya denotes absolute inaction or action without doership is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: O lord of knowledge, free from the distress of talk about agency and such, O lord of action, you remain as the excellence of non-action.

rows.grounds: compound: ignited by the chief among those worthy of remembrance
compound: lord of memory whose measure is the remembrance 'I'

items.question: What kind of remembrance establishes the lord of memory as measured by the awareness 'I'?
premises: Remembrance has a foremost object.
That foremost remembrance kindles awareness.
The lord of memory is measured by 'I'-remembrance.
items.inference: The supreme remembrance is the self-luminous 'I', which kindles and measures all memory.
uncertainties: The exact referent of smartavya-mukhya may be a specific deity or the self.
items.plain_english: Kindled by the foremost among those to be remembered, O lord of memory whose measure is the remembrance 'I'.

rows.grounds: compound vocative: sole cause of uplifting the play of threefold sovereignty shining in the sport within supreme atom and māyā

items.question: What single cause uplifts the play of threefold sovereignty within the supreme atom and māyā?
premises: Threefold sovereignty manifests as play.
This play shines within the supreme atom and māyā.
Such uplifting requires a sole cause.
items.inference: The addressed lord alone is the cause that uplifts and manifests the play of sovereignty within limitation.
uncertainties: The precise technical sense of traiśvarya in this context is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: O sole cause of the uplifting play of threefold sovereignty, shining in sport within the supreme atom and māyā.

rows.grounds: vocative compound: sovereign of the vairāja realm
compound vocative: bearer of the kingdom shining in the assembly of being one's own mother

items.question: How does the king of vairāja bear a kingdom grounded in the state of being one's own mother?
premises: The lord is king of vairāja.
A state of being one's own mother is honored.
This honored state constitutes a kingdom borne by the lord.
items.inference: The lord's sovereignty includes the self-generative, maternal aspect of consciousness as its kingdom.
uncertainties: The metaphor of svajanitri-bhāva is doctrinally dense and open to layered readings.
items.plain_english: O king of vairāja, bearer of the kingdom honored in the assembly of the state of being your own mother.

rows.grounds: vocative addressing the lord as companion
compound vocative: ground of the wish-jewel of skill in the supreme play of self-concealment

items.question: Why is the mighty friend called the wish-jewel of skill in the play of self-concealment?
premises: The lord is addressed as friend and mighty.
Self-concealment is a supreme play.
Skill in this play functions like a wish-jewel.
items.inference: The lord's power to conceal himself is not a defect but a sovereign, wish-fulfilling skill.
uncertainties: The nuance of sayuk as a separate vocative-like qualifier is slightly ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Endowed and friendly, O mighty one, you are the wish-jewel of skill in the supreme play of self-concealment.

rows.grounds: compound vocative: to be realized through the pervasion of self-affirmation
compound vocative: wise one, giver of this, lord presiding over complete dissolution

items.question: How can the lord of complete dissolution be contemplated through the pervasion of self-affirmation?
premises: The lord presides over complete dissolution.
The lord is wise and a giver.
Contemplation occurs through pervasion of self-affirmation.
items.inference: Even dissolution is known and given through the pervasive self-awareness of 'I'.
uncertainties: The referent of etat-dā ('giver of this') is not specified.
items.plain_english: To be contemplated through the pervasion of self-affirmation, O wise giver of this, O lord of complete dissolution.

rows.grounds: compound vocative: one and many nature of the divisions of time-units made by time that fashions timeless units

items.question: How can one reality be both one and many as the nature of time and timeless divisions?
premises: Time produces divisions and units.
There are divisions beyond ordinary time.
The addressed reality is both one and many.
items.inference: The supreme nature underlies and unifies all temporal and atemporal divisions as both singular and manifold.
uncertainties: The internal parsing of the long compound allows multiple technical readings.
items.plain_english: O you who are the one and many nature of the divisions of time-units, fashioned by time beyond time.

rows.grounds: compound vocative: sole inscriber of self-delineation, erasure, writing, and what is written
vocative compound: self of the taijasa or luminous nature

items.question: What does it mean for the luminous self to be the sole inscriber of all writing and erasure?
premises: Delineation, erasure, writing, and the written occur.
There is a sole inscriber of these.
This inscriber is the luminous self.
items.inference: All manifestation and withdrawal are inscriptions made by the single luminous consciousness.
uncertainties: taijasa may allude to a specific doctrinal level or simply luminosity.
items.plain_english: O sole inscriber of self-delineation, erasure, writing, and the written, O luminous self.

rows.grounds: compound vocative: whose universal form has made lordlessness subservient by a fragment of unbroken sovereignty and awareness

items.question: How does a fragment of unbroken sovereignty make lordlessness subservient in the universal form?
premises: Sovereignty and awareness are unbroken.
Even a fragment of them has power.
Lordlessness is made subservient in the universal form.
items.inference: The universe's apparent lack of lordship is overcome by the inherent power of supreme sovereignty.
uncertainties: The sense of khaṇḍa as 'fragment' may be rhetorical rather than literal division.
items.plain_english: O you whose universal form has made lordlessness subservient by a fragment of unbroken sovereignty and awareness.

rows.grounds: vocative compound: sole root-bulb of the nectar of transcendent bliss
vocative compound: bliss arising from what is not bliss
vocative compound: great secret or mystery

items.question: How can transcendent bliss be both the root of nectar and bliss born of non-bliss?
premises: Transcendent bliss is a sole root of nectar.
Bliss can be described as born of non-bliss.
This paradox is a great mystery.
items.inference: Supreme bliss transcends ordinary oppositions, appearing even through what seems unlike bliss.
uncertainties: The paradoxical phrase na-ānanda-ja-ānanda admits multiple doctrinal interpretations.
items.plain_english: O sole root of the nectar of transcendent bliss, O bliss born of non-bliss, O great mystery.

rows.grounds: vocative: pervaded by the unattainable pervasiveness abiding in space
vocative compound: transcendence beyond limited or impaired pervasiveness

items.question: How is the lord pervaded by unattainable pervasiveness yet beyond impaired pervasiveness?
premises: Pervasiveness abiding in space is unattainable.
Ordinary pervasiveness can be impaired.
The lord transcends impaired pervasiveness.
items.inference: The lord's pervasion is absolute, surpassing both limited reach and conceptual grasp.
uncertainties: The relation between being pervaded and being transcendent is paradoxical in expression.
items.plain_english: O you pervaded by the unattainable pervasiveness abiding in space, O transcendence of impaired pervasiveness.

rows.grounds: compound: dust particles arisen from your lotus feet
compound in apposition: the powers of creation and dissolution

items.question: Why are the dust particles from the lord's lotus feet identified with the powers of creation and dissolution?
premises: Dust arises from the lord's lotus feet.
Creation and dissolution are powers.
These powers supremely triumph.
items.inference: Even the slightest trace of the lord embodies the victorious powers that create and dissolve the universe.
uncertainties: The apposition between dust and powers is metaphorical and may be read in multiple ways.
items.plain_english: The dust particles arisen from your lotus feet, which are the powers of creation and dissolution, triumph supremely.

rows.grounds: compound locative: in the poem named Nāmavilāsa
refers to two aspects or purposes fulfilled

items.question: What dual purpose does devotion fulfill in the composed poem named Nāmavilāsa?
premises: A poem named Nāmavilāsa has been composed.
Devotion is present in it.
This devotion fulfills two things.
items.inference: The devotional composition serves a twofold completion within the work Nāmavilāsa.
uncertainties: The exact two referents of dvayoḥ are not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: In the composed poem named Nāmavilāsa, devotion fulfills the two.

items.question: What marks the second devotion within the work called Nāmavilāsa?
premises: The work is Nāmavilāsa.
Devotion is being enumerated.
This is the second devotion.
items.inference: The text explicitly marks a second phase or form of devotion in Nāmavilāsa.
uncertainties: The content distinguishing this second devotion from the first is not stated here.
items.plain_english: In Nāmavilāsa, this is the second devotion.

items.question: Why is the lord's greatness beyond heart and speech yet still to be indicated?
premises: The greatness is not within range of heart and speech.
It may be considered expressible.
Even so it must be indicated.
items.inference: The lord's greatness transcends direct expression but can still be pointed to indirectly.
uncertainties: The concessive force of vācyo api is compact and interpretively delicate.
items.plain_english: This greatness of yours alone is not within the range of heart and speech; even if expressible, it can only be indicated.

rows.grounds: compound: independent, the accomplishment of all accomplishments
adjective: shining by its own light

items.question: How can consciousness triumph as both full and empty while remaining self-luminous and independent?
premises: Consciousness is independent and accomplishes all accomplishments.
It is described as full and also empty.
It is self-luminous and triumphant.
items.inference: Supreme consciousness transcends the opposition of fullness and emptiness through its self-luminous freedom.
uncertainties: The grammatical agreement across compounds suggests a unified description but is compressed.
items.plain_english: Consciousness, independent and the accomplishment of all accomplishments, though full yet empty, self-luminous, you triumph.

rows.grounds: locative compound: in the particular opened as the principle of the moment

items.question: How does the other dissolve in the lord within the particular that opens as the principle of the moment?
premises: What is other can dissolve in the lord.
A particular opens as the principle of the moment.
This dissolution occurs in that particular.
items.inference: Even momentary particularity is a locus where apparent otherness dissolves into the lord.
uncertainties: nimeṣa-tattva may carry a specific technical sense beyond 'moment'.
items.plain_english: Just as the other is dissolved in you, so too in the particular that has opened as the principle of the moment.

rows.grounds: object: the status of being an object

items.question: How can non-difference attain objecthood while self-knowledge devoid of particularity remains yours alone?
premises: The state of non-difference can appear as objecthood.
Self-knowledge is devoid of particularity.
Such self-knowledge belongs to the lord alone.
items.inference: Apparent objectification does not compromise the lord's unique, non-particular self-knowledge.
uncertainties: The syntax linking the two clauses is compact and allows slight variation in emphasis.
items.plain_english: The state of non-difference attains objecthood, yet self-knowledge devoid of particularity is yours alone.

rows.grounds: locative compound: here in the sole abode of experience

items.question: Why are valid and erroneous measures unfitting in the sole abode of direct experience?
premises: This is the sole abode of experience.
Valid measure and erroneous measure are epistemic tools.
Neither is fitting here.
items.inference: Direct experience as the ultimate abode transcends the applicability of both valid and invalid measurement.
uncertainties: The scope of māna/vimāna may include specific pramāṇa categories.
items.plain_english: Here, in the sole abode of experience, neither valid measure nor erroneous measure is fitting.

rows.grounds: absolutive: having made shine with your own form
adjective: appearing as causality and so on

items.question: How does the lord alone shine as this world by manifesting as causality and other forms?
premises: The lord alone is the agent.
The lord manifests this with his own form.
He shines as causality and other appearances.
items.inference: All appearances, including causality, are self-manifestations of the one lord.
uncertainties: The range implied by ādi after kāraṇatā is unspecified.
items.plain_english: You alone, having manifested this with your own form, shine by yourself, appearing as causality and so forth.

rows.grounds: compound: that which is other than this
rhetorical question: what connection with another is there here

items.question: If something other than this appears, what connection with another can it have if it is self-established?
premises: Something other than this may appear.
Whatever appears is self-established.
A connection with another would require dependence.
items.inference: Even apparent otherness has no real dependence on another, since it is self-established in appearance.
uncertainties: The force of svasiddhaṃ may be epistemic or ontological.
items.plain_english: If something other than this appears, that very thing is self-established; what connection with another could there be here?

rows.grounds: compound: for one who knows all through the reasoning of one's own statement
refers to that reasoning or knowledge
object: the status of being known

items.question: Why can no one else attain knowledge of the reasoning by which the all-knowing one knows all?
premises: One knows all through the reasoning of one's own statement.
Another might seek to know that reasoning.
No one attains the knownness of that reasoning.
items.inference: The self-validating knowledge of the all-knowing consciousness cannot be objectified by another.
uncertainties: The antecedent of tasyā is slightly ambiguous between reasoning and knowledge.
items.plain_english: For one who knows all through the reasoning of one's own statement, no one else attains knowledge of that.

rows.grounds: rhetorical question: what follows from that
compound: one who shares in enjoyment and liberation

items.question: If even this is not attained, what contrary result prevents one from sharing in enjoyment and liberation?
premises: Even this may not be attained.
One might expect a contrary consequence.
A knower can partake of enjoyment and liberation.
items.inference: Failure to attain this does not necessarily produce a contrary outcome that blocks participation in enjoyment and liberation.
uncertainties: The referent of eṣaḥ is not explicit in this verse.
items.plain_english: Even if this is not attained, what is contrary? One would still partake of knowledge, enjoyment, and liberation.

rows.grounds: refers to this state or teaching
compound: means for the knowledge of you

items.question: How does immersion in this state become the supreme means for knowing the lord with true bliss?
premises: Immersion in this is possible.
It is a supreme means.
It leads to knowledge of the lord with true bliss.
items.inference: Absorptive immersion is the highest method for attaining knowledge of the lord accompanied by true bliss.
uncertainties: The addressee mātari may be literal, devotional, or doctrinal.
items.plain_english: O mother, immersion in this, even when supreme, is the means for knowing you, accompanied by true bliss.
